## Structural map engine

Package **`internal/mapengine`** (module `github.com/gkoreli/ghx/v2`) implements ghx's structural code-mapping engine — the thing behind `ghx read --map`. It exposes a single entry point:

```go
func Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error)
```

Defined in `internal/mapengine/types.go`. There are three concrete mappers implementing the `Mapper` interface (`Map(path, content, opts) (Result, error)`):

| File | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/mapengine/goast.go` | `GoASTMapper` | Uses stdlib `go/parser` + `go/ast` to extract packages, imports, funcs, types, const/var decls from `.go` files. |
| `internal/mapengine/treesitter.go` | `TreeSitterMapper` | Uses the pure-Go, CGo-free `github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter` runtime with grammar `tags.scm` queries to extract symbols (`@definition.function`, `@definition.class`, etc.) for TS/TSX/JS/JSX/Python/Rust. |
| `internal/mapengine/regex.go` | `RegexMapper` | Per-language regex rule tables (`regexRules` map keyed by extension, e.g. `"go"`, `"ts"`, `"tsx"`) as a language-agnostic fallback. |

`types.go` also defines the shared `Symbol`/`Result` model and `buildResultFromSymbols`, which sorts/dedupes/formats symbols per the requested `Level` (`outline|minimal|compact|standard`) and `Kind` filter (`func|type|import|const|var|...`).

## Engine selection per file (`mapAuto`, in `types.go`)

`Map()` normalizes `opts.Engine` (`auto|regex|tree-sitter`; anything else collapses to `auto`) and dispatches:

- **`EngineRegex`** → forces `RegexMapper` directly.
- **`EngineTreeSitter`** → forces `TreeSitterMapper` via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., true)`, which falls back to regex (with a warning) if tree-sitter errors.
- **`EngineAuto`** (default) → `mapAuto(path, content, opts)` picks by file extension:
  - `.go` → `GoASTMapper`; if it errors, silently falls back to `RegexMapper` (marks `Fallback: true`).
  - `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `TreeSitterMapper` via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., false)`, falling back to regex if tree-sitter can't parse it (unsupported grammar) or errors.
  - any other extension → `RegexMapper` directly.
- Any unrecognized `opts.Engine` value → regex fallback with a warning (defensive default branch; unreachable in practice since `NormalizeOptions` already coerces to `auto`).

So: **Go files get native `go/ast`, TS/TSX/JS/JSX/Python/Rust get Tree-sitter, everything else gets regex — with tree-sitter and go/ast both degrading gracefully to regex on failure.**

## Call sites (how `--map` reaches the engine)

- `internal/ghx/read.go:187` — `Read()` calls `mapengine.Map(path, []byte(text), mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), Level: ..., Kind: ...})` when `ReadOpts.Map` is true.
- `internal/cli/ghx.go` (`readCmd`, ~line 108-121) — reads the `--map-engine`, `--level`, `--kind` cobra flags and populates `ghxlib.ReadOpts.MapEngine`.
- `internal/ghx/register.go` — same plumbing for the MCP tool surface (`mapEngine` argument in the tool schema/handler).

## Design rationale

`docs/adr/0013-ghx-map-command.md` documents why: GitHub's public GraphQL/REST APIs have no real code-search/symbol API, so ghx fetches raw files via documented APIs and parses them locally. Regex was demoted from "main value" to "fallback only" because it misses multi-line signatures, decorators, nested symbols, etc. Tree-sitter was chosen via `odvcencio/gotreesitter` specifically because it's pure Go / no CGo, preserving ghx's `CGO_ENABLED=0` static cross-compilation release model.

**What I did not verify:** I did not run the code or tests (no clone was done, per instructions), so behavior is based on static reading of source via `gh api`/`gh repo view` against the `mainline` branch. I did not inspect `treesitter.go` beyond its `Map` method and language-detection stub (`treeSitterEntry`), nor `regex.go` in full, nor the MCP `register.go` handler body beyond the grepped lines — there may be additional nuance (e.g., full list of tree-sitter language configs, exact regex rule sets for non-Go languages) not captured above.
